Method/Recombination filtering

Iterative recombination detection

Alternate between tree building and detecting regions of elevated SNP density until the result converges.

When to use this method

Use when

  • Samples are closely related, such as a single lineage or outbreak sharing a recent common ancestor.
  • You want a recombination-filtered alignment and a starting tree in one step.
  • No tree exists yet for your samples.

Use another method when

  • You need estimates of recombination parameters, such as the relative effect of recombination and mutation. Use Clonal frame inference instead.
  • The collection spans many distantly related lineages, where run time grows and detection becomes less reliable.

Operation

Recombination filtering

Implementations

  • Gubbins

Needs

Full genome alignment

Produces

Recombination-filtered alignment, Phylogenetic tree

Recombinant regions appear as clusters of substitutions on a branch. This method repeatedly builds a tree, flags those clusters, masks them, and rebuilds until no new regions are found.

Used by protocols

Specified by

  • Bacterial phylogenomic surveillanceStep 4 (optional)

Alternative methods

  • Clonal frame inferenceModel recombination along a fixed tree with a hidden Markov model and infer the clonal genealogy.
